data.name: Page.Parquet.RestorePointsHint
data.value: A point for each processed snapshot that a later run left behind by changing a table already loaded. Restoring one takes the whole pipeline back to that moment: every table that changed afterwards gets back the Parquet it had, tables that did not exist yet are archived, and the pipeline is rewound to that snapshot. SQL is reloaded only for the tables that go back, and the next run brings back the later rows if their snapshots are still in the lake. Points are kept for the days set in Settings, and the most recent one is always kept; it also undoes a restore.

data.name: Page.Parquet.NoRestorePoints
data.value: This pipeline has no restore points yet: they are created when a run changes a table that was already loaded.

data.name: Page.Parquet.RestoreBlocked

data.name: Page.Parquet.ConfirmRestore
data.value: Go back to snapshot {0}? {1} table(s) get back the Parquet they had and {2} that did not exist yet are archived. The current copies become versions (the most recent point undoes the restore) and SQL is reloaded for the tables that go back.

data.name: Page.Parquet.PendingReloadNote

data.name: Page.Parquet.Restored

data.name: Error.sql.login.Title
data.value: Could not sign in to SQL Server

data.name: Error.sql.login.Cause
data.value: The destination user or password is wrong, or the login is disabled.

data.name: Error.sql.login.Fix
data.value: Check the user and password in Destinations and press Test connection. With SQL authentication, make sure the server allows it.

data.name: Error.sql.database.Title
data.value: The destination database does not exist

data.name: Error.sql.database.Cause
data.value: The database does not exist or the user has no access to it.

data.name: Error.sql.database.Fix
data.value: Create the database (Sluice does not create it) or fix its name in Destinations, and grant the user access.

data.name: Error.sql.network.Cause
data.value: The server name does not resolve, the port is closed or a firewall blocks the connection.

data.name: Error.sql.network.Fix
data.value: Check the host and port in Destinations, that the server accepts TCP connections and that no firewall blocks the port (1433 by default).

data.name: Error.sql.timeout.Title
data.value: SQL Server took too long to respond

data.name: Error.sql.timeout.Cause
data.value: The connection or a query timed out, usually because of a slow network or a busy or blocked server.

data.name: Error.sql.timeout.Fix
data.value: Check the server load and any blocking, then use Retry.

data.name: Error.sql.deadlock.Cause
data.value: Another session was locking the same rows and SQL Server cancelled this operation to resolve it.

data.name: Error.sql.deadlock.Fix
data.value: It is usually transient: use Retry. If it repeats, check which other processes write to those tables at the same time.

data.name: Error.sql.logFull.Title
data.value: The destination transaction log is full

data.name: Error.sql.logFull.Cause
data.value: The database has no room left in its log to record the load.

data.name: Error.sql.logFull.Fix
data.value: Grow the log or the disk, or back up the log if the database uses the full recovery model, then use Retry.

data.name: Error.sql.duplicateKey.Title
data.value: Duplicate Id in the destination table

data.name: Error.sql.duplicateKey.Cause
data.value: The table already has a row with that Id.

data.name: Error.sql.duplicateKey.Fix
data.value: Re-sync the table from Tables (Reload mode) so it matches the Parquet.

data.name: Error.sql.truncated.Title
data.value: A value does not fit in the destination column

data.name: Error.sql.truncated.Cause
data.value: A value is longer than its SQL column, usually because the column type was changed by hand.

data.name: Error.sql.truncated.Fix
data.value: Restore the column type (or drop the table so Sluice creates it again) and run Force.

data.name: Error.sql.mergeDuplicateSource.Title
data.value: The MERGE received the same Id twice

data.name: Error.sql.mergeDuplicateSource.Cause
data.value: The table's consolidated Parquet has more than one row with the same Id (error 8672).

data.name: Error.sql.mergeDuplicateSource.Fix
data.value: Reset the pipeline (Pipelines → Reset) and run it to rebuild the Parquet.

data.name: Error.adls.forbidden.Title
data.value: No permission on the ADLS storage

data.name: Error.adls.forbidden.Cause
data.value: The connection identity has no permission on the container.

data.name: Error.adls.forbidden.Fix
data.value: Give the connection identity the Storage Blob Data Contributor role on the Synapse Link and Parquet containers (Reader is not enough: Sluice writes the Parquet and purges processed CSVs). Role changes can take a few minutes.

data.name: Error.adls.notFound.Title
data.value: ADLS container or path not found

data.name: Error.adls.notFound.Cause
data.value: The container or folder does not exist in the storage account.

data.name: Error.adls.notFound.Fix
data.value: Check the account name and the Synapse Link and Parquet container names in Sources.

data.name: Error.adls.auth.Title
data.value: The Azure credentials are not valid

data.name: Error.adls.auth.Cause
data.value: Entra ID rejected the connection: the secret expired or is wrong, or the tenant or client id do not match.

data.name: Error.adls.auth.Fix
data.value: Create a new secret in the app registration and update it in Sources; also check the tenant and client id.

data.name: Error.adls.host.Title
data.value: The storage account cannot be found

data.name: Error.adls.host.Cause
data.value: The ADLS account name does not resolve on the network.

data.name: Error.adls.host.Fix
data.value: Check the account name in Sources and that the machine can reach *.dfs.core.windows.net (or its private endpoint).
